 Judgment

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 11.03.2016.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 11.03.2016 he was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/Y-5384 (hereinafter referred as "the offending vehicle") as a pillion rider on Korwar road.
Near Muchkhed bridge, accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Inspite of prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
3.1. After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed chargesheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was aged 25 years and earning Rs.2,00,000/ p.a. by agriculture.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
As owner and insurer, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 remained ex parte.

5. Respondent 2 filed written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner,
nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
Respondent No.2 has also contended that since the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence, it is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 11.
Sangappa vs Devindrappa And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134304839/
2 8. Respondent No.2 has not led any oral and documentary evidence.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,04,500/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
1. Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
2. Loss of future income Rs.2,20,300/-
3. Medical expenditure Rs.64,200/-
4. Loss of amenities and nutrition Rs.10,000/-
food
Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted the appellant has suffered 50% disability of the whole body and 17% taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the fact that accident is of the year 2016, the notional income taken at Rs.6,000/- p.m. is on the lower side.
The compensating granted under other heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

13. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
14.
Based on the complaint lodged in respect of the accident, the concerned police have conducted detailed investigation and filed the chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
During the course of his evidence, the petitioner, who is examined as P.W.1 has deposed with regard to the accident and injuries suffered by him.

Taking into consideration the documents placed on record and the evidence of P.W.1, the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. Having regard to the grounds urged in the appeal memo, it is necessary to examine whether the compensation granted to the petitioner is just and reasonable or it calls for interference by this Court:
16. Based on the medical records, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 25 years and appropriate multiplier 18.
In the absence of proof of exact income, on notional basis, it has considered the income as Rs.6,000/-.

Since the accident is of the year 2016, the notional income Sangappa vs Devindrappa And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134304839/
3 is considered at Rs.8,750/- p.m.

Having regard to the fact that P.W.2 is not treating doctor and disability is not calculated in according to the prescribed norm, the Tribunal has justified in considering the whole body disability at 17%.

With these components, the compensation under the head loss of future income is Rs.8,750/- x 12 x 18 x 17%= Rs.3,21,300/- as against Rs.2,20,300/-
granted by the Tribunal.

17. Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered resulting in permanent partial disability,
Rs.10,000/- each granted under the head pain and suffering & loss of amenities is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/- and Rs.20,000 respectively.

18. Having regard to the fact that the injuries suffered are grievous and they have resulted in permanent partial disability, it would be natural to expect that the petitioner was under treatment for three months and therefore, at the rate of Rs.8,750/- p.m., he is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.26,250/- under the head loss of income during laid up period, Rs.20,000/- under the head food, nutrition and attendant charges.

19. Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.64,200/-
and it requires no interference.

Since the petitioner has undergone surgery for further treatment and suffered permanent partial disability, it would be appropriate to grant Rs.20,000/-.
20.
Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.5,21,750/- together with interest at 6% p.a., as against Rs.3,04,500/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

 sufferings

2. Loss of Rs.10,000/- Rs.20,000/-
 amenities of life (Loss of  amenities and  nutrition food)

3. Medical Rs.64,200/- Rs.64,200/-
 expenses 4.

Loss of income Rs.2,20,300/- Rs.3,21,300/-
 due to disability 5. Compensation -- Rs.26,250/-
 for the laid up  period 6. Food, nutrition -- Rs.20,000/-
 and attendant  charges 7.

Future medical -- Rs.20,000/-
 expenses

Total Rs.3,04,500/- Rs.5,21,750/-

4 21.
Of course as the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the enhanced compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,21,750/- as against Rs.3,04,500/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a.
(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest.

(Minus the compensation already paid/deposited)
(iv) Send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
